I don't know what 'meta' means, but, if you're talking about topics like the one you've brought up in this post, the suitable subverse would either be this one or /v/ideasforwhoaverse. I don't see /v/AskWhoa having an exclusive personality like AskReddit has on Reddit, so I see this subverse as one where these questions are welcomed.

A large problem of Reddit was that the quality of posts and comments became worse over time because of people trying to gain more karma.

I'm possibly misunderstanding you, so I'll need you to clarify in the case I assume falsely. With that said, I'll make the point that,

  • The need of an incentive to make valuable contributions to a discussion outweighs the problems that 'karma-whoring' causes.

Usually, in situations like these, a compromise needs to be made that accounts for all factors on both sides of the argument. Yes, karma-whoring can negatively impact a community, but the feature that indirectly causes this issue is one that a community like WhoaVerse needs in order to sustain a healthy community.

Additionally, which also leads to my second point, one of the reasons that a compromise like this must exist for the time being is that,

  • A better system to maintain a healthy community does not exist yet to rid the problem of 'karma-whoring', so improvements to the current system should be the main focus in order to ensure the vitality of the community survives long enough to find a better system.

I feel that one of the main reasons 'karma-whoring' can still exist is that we haven't crafted a better system to handle contributions. The focus of the solution, then, is not to try to change the system to cease the existance of 'karma-whoring', which could be an impossibility within a reasonable amount of time, but to maintain the vitality of the current system until we find a better way to handle discussions.

Really though, I'm just trying to start a discussion to see how we can change this site to make it like Reddit but without it's problems.

These types of discussions are more than welcome here on WhoaVerse. Since it's still in its early stages, there is more than enough time to shape the community into something beautiful. Whether or not it can eventually be defined as "better than Reddit" isn't certain, but I'm sure it'll be a site we will all enjoy.
You understood me perfectly! I have to say, this is incredibly well written and well formatted. I completely agree with everything you said.

If I may add one thing on my own accord, it is that we have had a few problematic "power-users" that had a self-entitlement aura with every comment reply and WhoaVerse chewed them up and spit them out. I'd like to say that the community we have now is very protective over this site. And for good reason. A lot of the people here have shaped what it has become and don't want it to become some vague memory. We want this to be an awesome site, rich with fresh content, great people, and true to the original idea that Atko has. Power users that are only here for points, as if they actually matter, don't and won't last long.

My only fear is that one day the population here will surge and that this new found popularity will bring a lot of bad content, and this place will be littered with low quality content much like Reddit. I left Reddit specifically because of the large amount of bad posts. I still go on it from time to time, and I'm subbed to many niche subreddits because I'm trying to avoid bad content, but on more popular subreddits like /r/pics you'll see a lot of bad content. Usually default subs have this problem, but it extends very far throughout Reddit. I don't want to see that happen to WhoaVerse, but I do want to see it grow in popularity. This is a good opportunity to make a community content sharing site that has the perks of 4Chan and Reddit and the likes while also removing their issues. I think Nurdoidz is very much correct in saying that we need to develop a better system to maintain a healthy community, and a good one doesn't really exist on the internet yet.
